title: Segmentation CLI gaps, round 2: control fires tool-switch actions, regions are readable on screen, and the ring tool lists its rings as items
description:
Found by the CRAW-77 pilot segmenter (round 1), before round 2 (user approved 2026-10-24).
1. `tools` lists the tool-switch rows with action ids (e.g. `region-tool`), but `control --action region-tool` refuses them: since TOOL-41 the switch rows are their own section of Scene.controls and FireControl does not search it. control searches every section it lists.
2. Which region is where on screen: the agent can read screenshots, but they show colours only, so it matched regions to numbers with a 1,024-point `pick` grid (~45 s a view). First try the UI way: a region tool view toggle that draws each region's number (and part name, which CRAW-42 already draws) at its visible centre, so the number is read off the screenshot. If that is not enough, add to each region item its on-screen centre in window pixels and whether it is visible from the current camera (Tool-base item values, no new route).
3. The ring tool's items list is empty even with rings loaded, so ring details are only reachable through region detail text: the ring tool's items are its confirmed rings and bisectors (label, serial, mode, edge count, length, bounding regions), through the Tool base like every other tool.

SCOPE ADDED (user, 2026-10-24, after review): items are handles, datasets carry the data. (a) One confirmed-ring object replaces RingTool's eight parallel confirmed* lists (spline, mode, serial, bisector walls, statement id, source label, unsaved, deleted), used by items, undo state and saving. (b) Item is a handle: the common fields plus a kind (ring, bisector, region, path, neck, segment); the numbers/points/flags maps added in CRAW-75 are removed and detail stays a short human line. Domain data (region flatness and area, ring mode/serial/walls, connection girths) is exported by ixdar.automation from the scene's typed datasets (Scene.dataset), once per dataset type, not copied into items by each tool. The ring item stops listing the regions it bounds (the region items' bounding rings already say it). The region-number placement and the perFrame split are CRAW-78's.
definition-of-done:
1. `control --action <tool-switch id>` switches tools; a test covers it.
2. An agent can name the region under any point of a screenshot without pick calls (shown on IMG_4111).
3. The ring tool's items list every ring and bisector with its details.
4. Java and test_cli tests; gen-docs if routes change.
testing-plan:
1. mvn test, test_cli.
2. Live on a tmp copy of IMG_4111.
changes-made: FireControl (control route) searches the tool-switch section of Scene.controls too, so control --action region-tool switches tools (ToolInputReplyTest.aToolSwitchRowFiresByItsActionIdAndSwitchesTools).

Region numbers on screen, the UI way (no item values added): region tool row toggle-region-numbers (shift+N) makes RegionLayer place 'R<n>' at the thickest visible part of each region, found from a coarse face-id pass (new HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.faceIndexGrid, sharing the id-pass code with faceIndexAtPixel) and a chamfer distance; RingScene draws them, recomputed when the camera, regions or hidden faces change. The words route lists them with pixels too. Test: RegionControlAutomationTest.theRegionNumbersRowDrawsEachSeenRegionsNumberInsideTheViewOfIt. Live: IMG_4111 pick at R209's pixel returned region 209.

RingTool.items() returns every confirmed ring and bisector via ringItem, which now carries kind (closed ring/bisector), mode, bounded regions in detail, and serial plus a bisector's end-wall serials as values; RegionLayer.rings() removed (ui-state 'rings' reads ringTool.items()). Test: RingEscapeTest.theRingToolsItemsNameEachRingsSerialModeKindAndTheRegionsItBounds. Live: tools lists 82 ring items on IMG_4111 (was 0).

Rework after review (items are handles, datasets carry the data): a new ConfirmedRing class (ixdar.tools.ring) holds each confirmed ring or bisector's spline, anchors, normal, mode, statement, source label, unsaved, deleted, serial and wall serials; it replaces RingTool's ten parallel confirmed* lists in items, RingToolState undo snapshots (copied per ring), saving, reopening and both sub-tools. Fingerprints and saved .dsl byte-identical before/after on tmp copies of fertility_rings and IMG_4111 (draft, confirm, undo, redo, save).

Item is a handle: kind added (ring, bisector, region, path, neck, segment, city, route), numbers/points/flags removed, detail short; RingRegionTool, ConnectionTool, RoutePlanningTool items and drafts updated; RingRegions.flatnessText and PERCENT dropped (no callers). ui-state exports the RINGS dataset once: regions.rows (area, boundingRings with side, part, creaseShare, interiorCreaseShare, peakCurvature, peakOverSaturation, creasePoint, creaseInterior), rings (label, liveLabel, kind, mode, serial, statement, source, wallSerials, anchor counts, unsaved, deleted) and connection (girths, path). Tests: RegionControlAutomationTest.uiStateExportsTheRegionAndRingDatasetsOnceAndTheItemsAsHandles, RingEscapeTest.theRingToolsItemsAreHandlesOnItsConfirmedRings; RegionFlatnessTest reads RingRegions directly.
review-summary: FireControl fires tool switches, the region tool can draw region numbers on screen, RingTool keeps one ConfirmedRing per ring and lists them as items, and items become handles while ui-state exports the region, ring and connection datasets. Agents switch tools, read regions off screenshots and read ring data directly.
